headline.headline: WEMBANYAMA HANDS MVP GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER A LESSON IN OKLAHOMA CITY
headline.deck: Spurs stun top-seeded Thunder 122-115, seize Game 1 edge in Western semis
headline.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY -- Victor Wembanyama walked into Paycom Center on Monday night, waited while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accepted his second consecutive MVP trophy at center court, and then proceeded to dismantle the league's best record with 48 minutes of basketball the Thunder had no answer for. San Antonio's 122-115 victory gave the sixth-seeded Spurs a 1-0 series lead over a 64-win Oklahoma City team that came in as the prohibitive Western Conference favorite.

Gilgeous-Alexander, fresh from the pregame ceremony, acknowledged afterward that the performance was not what the moment demanded. The Thunder star, who averaged 32.7 points per game during the regular season, was held well below his standard output as Wembanyama's length disrupted passing lanes and altered shots at the rim. San Antonio's offense ran through Wembanyama with the kind of varied attack that masked his rookie limitations just two seasons ago but now looks like a genuine championship formula.

Game 2 remains in Oklahoma City, giving the Thunder an urgent chance to regroup before the series shifts to San Antonio. Coach Mark Daigneault's squad has the talent to bounce back, but the Spurs -- who finished second in the West at 62-20 -- have now beaten the top seed on its home floor and carry the psychological advantage into midweek. The basketball world is watching to see whether Gilgeous-Alexander can make good on his four-word postgame promise.

secondary.headline: SABRES' RENAISSANCE SEASON ENDS IN HEARTBREAK AS CANADIENS WIN GAME 7 IN OT
secondary.deck: Buffalo's emotional playoff run falls one win short; Montreal advances to third round
secondary.body:
BUFFALO -- The KeyBank Center crowd gave the Buffalo Sabres a standing ovation that lasted several minutes after Monday's 3-2 overtime loss to the Montreal Canadiens ended their remarkable second-round run, a scene more fitting of a championship sendoff than an elimination night. The Sabres, who missed the playoffs for more than a decade before this season's resurgence, pushed the Canadiens to the limit before falling in sudden death of Game 7.

Montreal now advances to the conference finals, having survived a Buffalo team that refused to concede the series at any point. The Sabres' fans, who endured years of rebuilding, flooded social media and the streets outside the arena with tributes to a group that restored credibility to a franchise starved for postseason hockey. The loss stings, but the foundation laid this spring in western New York points toward something larger in the seasons ahead.

secondary.headline: PROSPECT COLT EMERSON ANNOUNCES HIMSELF WITH THREE-RUN HOMER IN MARINERS WIN
secondary.deck: Seattle's touted rookie slugs first career hit out of the park as Woo dominates White Sox
secondary.body:
CHICAGO -- Colt Emerson could not have scripted a more dramatic introduction to the major leagues. The Seattle Mariners' most hyped positional prospect stepped to the plate in the early going Monday and launched a three-run home run for his first career hit, setting the tone for a 6-1 demolition of the Chicago White Sox at Guaranteed Rate Field. Bryan Woo backed the performance with a dominant outing on the mound, keeping Chicago's lineup quiet through the bulk of the game.

Emerson's blast sent the Seattle dugout into a frenzy and gave the Mariners exactly the offensive spark a pitching-dependent roster has craved. The young infielder had arrived in the big leagues carrying enormous expectations after tearing through the minor league system, and he answered with the kind of swing that scouts had long described in superlatives. For a Mariners club fighting to stay relevant in the American League West, Emerson's arrival may be the most significant development of the young summer.

secondary.headline: CARDINALS OPEN OTAs WITHOUT BRISSETT AS LAFLEUR ERA BEGINS IN ARIZONA
secondary.deck: New head coach Mike LaFleur launches first organized team activities amid quarterback uncertainty
secondary.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Arizona Cardinals opened organized team activities Monday under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur, but the quarterback situation that has shadowed the franchise all spring remained pointedly unresolved. Jacoby Brissett was absent from the field, and LaFleur told reporters that contract discussions sit in the same place they occupied weeks ago, a non-answer that did little to quiet speculation about who will take snaps under center when the regular season arrives.

LaFleur, the former offensive coordinator stepping into his first head-coaching role, is installing a new system in Arizona and needs clarity at the most important position to make it function. The Cardinals finished last season with significant questions at quarterback, and the OTA opener confirmed those questions have not been answered. Around the league, teams are deep into offseason programs, meaning Arizona's uncertain situation at the position draws sharper contrast with franchises that have already settled their depth charts.

column.headline: SGA'S TROPHY NIGHT BECAME WEMBANYAMA'S COMING-OUT PARTY
column.body:
There is a cruel irony in the way Monday played out in Oklahoma City. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander stood at center court and received the most coveted individual award in basketball for the second consecutive season, the crowd roaring, the confetti still settling, the whole ceremony designed to confirm his place among the game's giants. Then the opening tip came, and Victor Wembanyama began his answer. By the final buzzer, the MVP trophy felt less like a coronation and more like a target painted on the Thunder's chest. The Spurs did not come to watch the ceremony. They came to ruin it.

Wembanyama is not yet 23 years old, and he is already forcing the sport to rewrite its language. The question coming into these playoffs was whether San Antonio had enough supporting cast to compete with Oklahoma City's depth and experience. One game is not a series, and the Thunder will not go quietly, but the Spurs answered that question loudly enough to be heard clear across the league. If Gilgeous-Alexander truly intends to be better in Game 2, he will need to be the best player on the floor in a building where, for one night at least, that title belonged to someone else entirely.

story.headline: MARLINS BLANK BRAVES 12-0, METS MAUL NATIONALS 16-7 IN MONDAY SLUGFEST
story.deck: Miami stuns Atlanta with a mercy-rule rout while New York piles on Washington in a wild night
story.body:
MIAMI — The Miami Marlins delivered the most stunning result of the young baseball week Monday night, throttling the first-place Atlanta Braves 12-0 at loanDepot Park in a shutout that left the NL East leaders looking every bit as rattled as the final score suggested. Miami's pitching staff held Atlanta's lineup — one of the most productive in the National League — completely scoreless across nine innings, while the Marlins' bats erupted for 12 runs in what amounted to a statement win for a club sitting fourth in the division at 22-26.

The carnage extended north to New York, where the Mets hammered the Washington Nationals 16-7 at Citi Field in a game that never felt close after the early innings. New York's offense rolled through Washington's pitching staff with relentless efficiency, pushing the Mets deeper into postseason conversation while the Nationals continued to absorb punishment in what has become a difficult stretch on the road. The twin blowouts on the same evening marked a wild night across the National League.

Elsewhere Monday, the Cleveland Guardians extended their winning ways with an 8-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers, keeping their grip on first place in the AL Central at 27-22. The Philadelphia Phillies edged the Cincinnati Reds 5-4 in a tighter contest, and the New York Yankees survived a scare in Toronto, slipping past the Blue Jays 7-6 to avoid a series setback. The Tampa Bay Rays also put on an offensive showcase, routing the Baltimore Orioles 16-6 in a game that matched the Mets' run total and underscored just how much firepower was on display across the sport Monday evening.

story.headline: WEMBANYAMA, SPURS SILENCE MVP THUNDER IN OKLAHOMA CITY
story.deck: San Antonio steals Game 1 on the road, 122-115, stunning Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the top seed
story.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY — Victor Wembanyama walked into Paycom Center on Monday night as a 22-year-old alien presence in a building ready to crown its king, and he walked out with a statement. The San Antonio Spurs, 62-win second seeds who spent the regular season lurking in the shadow of the league's glamour franchise, dismantled the Oklahoma City Thunder 122-115 in Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals, stunning a sellout crowd that had gathered to celebrate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's second consecutive MVP award before tip-off.

Gilgeous-Alexander received his trophy in a pregame ceremony dripping with confetti and ceremony, then spent the next two and a half hours being reminded that hardware means nothing once the ball goes up. The Thunder star finished with strong numbers but was visibly frustrated down the stretch, and said afterward that he simply has to be better. Wembanyama, meanwhile, was a problem at both ends — protecting the rim, triggering the fast break, and punishing mismatches in the mid-post with the kind of fluid, unhurried brilliance that has made him the most discussed player on the planet since his rookie season.

San Antonio's victory gives the Spurs a 1-0 series lead against a Thunder team that posted the NBA's best record at 64-18. Oklahoma City, which had been installed as the heavy favorite to reach the Finals, now faces the uncomfortable reality that Wembanyama and Gregg Popovich's rebuilt machine may be precisely the matchup they least wanted. Game 2 is Wednesday night in Oklahoma City, where the Thunder will need a response or risk watching this series tilt toward the underdog with alarming speed.

boxScores.title: San Antonio Spurs 122, Oklahoma City Thunder 115

story.headline: NEWHOOK STRIKES AGAIN IN OT, SENDS CANADIENS TO THIRD ROUND WITH GAME 7 WIN OVER SABRES
story.deck: Montreal forward's overtime winner ends Buffalo's storybook renaissance season in heartbreak.
story.body:
MONTREAL — Alex Newhook has made overtime Game 7s his personal stage. The Colorado-born forward rifled home the winner in sudden death Monday night, lifting the Montreal Canadiens past the Buffalo Sabres 3-2 and punching Montreal's ticket to the third round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs. The Bell Centre shook with a roar that rattled rafters as Newhook's shot found the back of the net, silencing the traveling contingent of Sabres faithful who had dared to believe this was finally Buffalo's year.

The Sabres had done everything asked of them through a remarkable renaissance campaign, trading blows with Montreal through 60 minutes of tense, physical hockey. Buffalo tied the game in the third period to force overtime, riding the emotion of a fanbase that had waited decades for a postseason run worth remembering. But Newhook, who now owns two Game 7 overtime goals in a single postseason, proved to be the cruelest kind of executioner — brilliant, precise, and utterly without mercy when the moment demanded it.

For the Sabres, the 3-2 overtime defeat in Game 7 closes a season that will nonetheless be remembered as a turning point for the long-suffering franchise. Buffalo's players left the ice to a standing ovation from their own supporters, a small consolation after coming so close. The Canadiens, meanwhile, move on with momentum surging and Newhook operating at a level that has the rest of the Eastern Conference on notice.

story.headline: VETERANS CHANGE ADDRESSES AS NFL FREE AGENCY RESHAPES ROSTERS AHEAD OF TRAINING CAMP
story.deck: Big names land new deals while draft picks prepare to compete for starting jobs
story.body:
The NFL landscape looks dramatically different this May than it did when the Philadelphia Eagles hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at Super Bowl LX in February, with front offices across the league spending the spring reshuffling rosters in pursuit of championship-caliber talent. Quarterback movement has dominated the headlines, as veteran signal-callers Russell Wilson and Sam Darnold secured multi-year contracts with clubs desperate for experienced leadership under center. The Dallas Cowboys made the loudest splash of the offseason, trading a package of picks to acquire a proven pass rusher who figures to anchor their rebuilt defensive front for years to come.

The 2026 NFL Draft delivered its share of instant impact players, and scouts around the league believe several first-round selections are ready to start from day one. The Tennessee Titans, picking near the top of the order, addressed their long-standing offensive line deficiencies with back-to-back selections that drew praise from nearly every evaluator in the business. Running back depth was raided heavily in the middle rounds, as teams adjusting to the league's evolving offensive schemes stockpiled athletic options out of the backfield.

With mandatory minicamps wrapping up across the country and voluntary workouts well underway, coaches are already sorting through heated position battles that will define the character of their 2026 rosters. The New England Patriots, still rebuilding under their second-year head coach, generated genuine buzz when rookie wide receiver Marcus Bellamy hauled in touchdown after touchdown during organized team activities this week in Foxborough. Training camps open in late July, and between now and then, the transaction wire shows no sign of slowing down.
